mechanism_narrative: The recent rise in WORKPLACES alongside weaker TRANSIT and PARKS indicates a shift toward weekday destination trips rather than discretionary out-of-home time, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as routine errands and lunch shopping recover.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to improve but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-weeks mean within 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline while TRANSIT stays deeply negative, household substitution toward local shopping should raise neighborhood retail activity, producing a short-run increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if TRANSIT stays below -40 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 14 days relative to the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between improving transit access and higher workplace attendance should translate into more retail footfall only when both move together; if TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise, RETAIL_REC should increase within four weeks, but the effect should vanish if either series stalls.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both trend upward for two weeks and RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the following 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A broad shift into parks and away from transit is consistent with weather or seasonal outdoor substitution that diverts discretionary time from stores; under this pattern, RETAIL_REC should soften over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS rises while TRANSIT remains depressed and RETAIL_REC nevertheless increases over the next 28 days, the seasonal substitution claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise while RETAIL_REC stays below baseline, consumers are reallocating spending toward essentials, which should crowd out discretionary retail visits and keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 7 points and remains there for two weeks
failure_condition: The hypothesis is rejected if GROCERY_PHARM stays above 7 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not decline versus its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in TRANSIT combined with only a mild improvement in WORKPLACES means commuting returns are incomplete, so retail visits should remain constrained and RETAIL_REC should drift lower over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls week-on-week while WORKPLACES stays below -10
failure_condition: If TRANSIT weakens and WORKPLACES remains below -10 but RETAIL_REC rises in the following week, this short-horizon mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL eases back toward baseline while WORKPLACES improves, households are spending less time at home and more time near commercial corridors, which should support a higher RETAIL_REC level over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for two consecutive weeks from an elevated level
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls from an elevated level and WORKPLACES improves but RETAIL_REC does not increase over 28 days, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rebound in PARKS from very depressed levels signals warmer-weather discretionary activity, which typically spills into nearby shopping trips; if PARKS keeps recovering, RETAIL_REC should improve over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from its prior weekly mean
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by 5 points or more and RETAIL_REC still fails to outperform its last-2-weeks mean over the next 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
